items.stem: In Unity, what is the correct relationship between a GameObject and a component such as a script?

options.text: A component (including a script) is attached to a GameObject to give it behaviour or data
options.rationale: Correct: GameObjects are containers; components attached to them provide behaviour and data.

options.text: A GameObject is attached to a component
options.rationale: This reverses the relationship; components are added to GameObjects, not the other way round.

options.text: A script runs independently of any GameObject in the scene
options.rationale: A MonoBehaviour script only runs when attached to an active GameObject.

options.text: Components can exist in a scene without any GameObject
options.rationale: Components cannot exist on their own; they must belong to a GameObject.

items.explanation: Correct: GameObjects are containers; components attached to them provide behaviour and data.
items.domain_ref: Unity Editor, GameObjects and the C# Scripting Basics

items.stem: Why is a movement value commonly multiplied by Time.deltaTime in Update()?

options.text: To make movement speed independent of the frame rate
options.rationale: Correct: Time.deltaTime is the time since the last frame, so multiplying by it gives consistent speed regardless of frame rate.

options.text: To make the object move exactly one unit per frame
options.rationale: That would make speed depend on frame rate, which is what deltaTime avoids.

options.text: To convert the value from radians to degrees
options.rationale: Time.deltaTime has nothing to do with angle unit conversion.

options.text: To pause the game when the frame rate drops
options.rationale: deltaTime scales motion; it does not pause anything.

items.explanation: Correct: Time.deltaTime is the time since the last frame, so multiplying by it gives consistent speed regardless of frame rate.

items.stem: Select TWO conditions that must be true for OnTriggerEnter to be called between two objects in Unity.

options.text: At least one of the two colliders has 'Is Trigger' enabled
options.rationale: Correct: trigger callbacks require at least one collider marked Is Trigger.

options.text: At least one of the objects has a Rigidbody component
options.rationale: Correct: trigger/collision messages require a Rigidbody on at least one of the participating objects.

options.text: Both objects must have the same tag
options.rationale: Tags are optional filters in code; they are not required for the callback to fire.
Static objects without a Rigidbody will not generate trigger callbacks.

options.text: Both colliders must have 'Is Trigger' disabled
options.rationale: That describes a physical collision (OnCollisionEnter), not a trigger.

items.explanation: Correct: trigger callbacks require at least one collider marked Is Trigger.
